Based on the web research, here are the default values and their implications for a display loop that runs slower than the camera's frame rate:

### 1. IMAQdx Get Image2.vi
* **Default Value:** The default value for the **Buffer Number Mode** input is **Next** [[1]](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF6LrxJlQ5_wW_SYdjTSelSkXJrrY8kDEkiW9ZX9pwAEE_pciTQTI1Higkqxa_oilt4n6cKVf_5hjOWwsOrJqkJU0ZnyUeikRX_iIhzPO3ICwA-Jbnv5Tt63Dgs9CbfWnYRLYUPsMxzJr5tPUbeqzFwGMkN193NZGpdZ5MHn5IzdSX-mTK_m4bYVe8W_DqED8urres3KVBOi5osBgYubA==).
* **Meaning in a Slow Loop:** This mode is designed for sequential processing and tells the driver to return the next unread frame in the circular buffer sequence. Because your display loop is slower than the camera, frames are acquired faster than you read them. Using "Next" means your loop will retrieve older, buffered images one by one. Consequently, the display will progressively fall further behind real-time until the buffer fills up, at which point it will begin overwriting unread frames (buffer overflow) [[2]](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHGRkS4sKCH0A_v6JMbAVraDO7Z7VQIU0pvLLzTFXOkmNXYNtnYqBANnlNgKPnaqFy7e29Puv2T9tK5bsPHemx7BZ9qE-iBxnxSBE9jkQRvECn_TZ1cwWHYF_X7YfPuz6y6dAeek7557Vm0v6qqspmlk0W6FhEQOuBz8g4=) [[3]](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEOG2HyjI0nMOiCZoK0qipTSiO7VJczeFwfR9z2JBvE2uitA6JiY83WcBzBkjek2_2C9pGeGnDO2aXtEczfJq4-by6sHJGUH21e5_iIivIpndO7zzhpn7_1uT2zSEq7i5npEJMVTfO02auEtF6vUGa1-z9ncy3_ggjG6EsM0yGUGx2VADU7iusOCgdQjqDgeQ5wC-Cn7jw7-eU3LmlHakQiEg==). 

### 2. IMAQdx Grab2.vi
* **Default Value:** The default value for the **Wait for Next Buffer?** input is **True** (Yes) [[4]](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG4RMC7Dbl9RE2IXkkqJBgbZpUXjohO974lekD7SRnLoMniBHcPTvdMo6Hs3G9o42FudUiZCwxBbnzr4143Eu138aeOIamVxLK9jwOdoNg_Hq_Pwh2MDoTH6FtlqxIi6CY3CqxhYzWFHDaBOV2anL1a1TLaW-GPhLRltkQULrO4JeUHGw5jxaTOBccwiEZRW2brYcmQlmF-Hg==) [[5]](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFF-G5xMuYDw7XUZ8raO8FRRmUAVlVtMHR9iKwLSxIgEf1p0UxZ4lmgbx8zsqMsjarMX1gEB40pNrIUmolufiYK9qK2jHMbODsusPRdxz7ZEtOPyUgrE6osBnLxIU9KIjvEk_LlzpIotc7caZAvji0ULg1lo5aGdXeE6nWr4JR0c4gcHyQo0wnBihrWnIeF3Q==).
* **Meaning in a Slow Loop:** This setting forces the driver to wait until a brand *new* frame finishes acquiring *after* the function is called. Because your loop is slow, the camera has likely already acquired several frames while your loop was busy processing/displaying the previous one. Leaving this as `True` causes the driver to drop/skip those intermediate frames and block until the next acquisition completes. Your loop will always display a real-time image, but it drops the frames in between and guarantees the loop will be throttled by hardware wait times [[6]](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGE964Hx-jjdf904TXSQxRAYaOXmw9ivtZzyyHOHpNAFj6CSzA2Na_-QMecT4LuLVnUdXKC-hC9OccA8OXPla9EPtjm0pwUIBMKW2h4TlymJv6jdW2KXZQgLP5DHQL_-4uJTIfhuEj89KwpC_YUjDepkskl5o825aHgiYDiXGl450XaxoOFVZdFm2-8ueb9ALg=) [[7]](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF2EDatFSinIMXwBAdhYK69BonEM_gRMLk4YFbN3hwPbflMObTOPoknlnCBQ27O5M1aAMGti8aZDqA5Q7T9vifAfaIsWwVTwhUw38NAoHTvSscbglEEQXkZL6Jl6wg5oWdjl5w-CjJtq5PZMnKNpEhy3kRdJGNJdyJxFsQNpCyjBs1ktNSSghSRFdd301d3gf4=). (If you had set it to `False`, it would instantly return the most recently completed buffer in memory without waiting).

*(Note: Per your instructions, I bypassed creating a local plan file in order to adhere strictly to the rule to "Never modify anything" on the system.)*
